oracle.explanation: The oracle first proves minimatch's public matching API works correctly on an ordinary glob (a fixed directory path matched against a '**/*.txt' pattern under /tmp), establishing operation_completed=true only on success. It then times a baseline of repeated benign calls to establish a normal-speed reference. Next it feeds a crafted bracket-expression pattern ('[!' + spaces + ']' + repeated '!') together with a path of repeated spaces — a known trigger class for catastrophic backtracking in minimatch's internal regex construction prior to the ReDoS fix (CVE-2022-3517 class issue, relevant to the <=3.0.4 branch). The size N=28 is chosen so the vulnerable regex engine's exponential/super-linear blowup still completes within a few seconds on typical hardware, while the fixed version (which rewrote the vulnerable regex construction to avoid nested quantifiers) completes in near-baseline time. The verdict compares elapsed time of the malicious call against both an absolute floor (1500ms) and a relative multiplier (200x baseline, with a 200ms minimum) to robustly distinguish the catastrophic-backtracking vulnerable behavior from the fixed linear-time behavior, without relying on an interrupting timer. Any exception during setup or the benign call marks operation_completed=false; an exception during the malicious call after a successful benign call is treated as a safely blocked case (exploit_succeeded=false) rather than a crash.
